options.text: The speed exceeds the circular speed, so the path becomes elliptical or escapes.

options.text: Only the solid sphere has zero field at its centre.

options.text: Only the hollow sphere has zero field at its centre.
options.misconception: thinks solid spheres have nonzero centre field

options.text: Both centres have zero field, but for different reasons.

questions.explanation: Both centres have zero net field: the hollow sphere by shell cancellation, the solid sphere by symmetry and the linear interior law.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_MECHANICS
questions.topic: Field inside a uniform sphere
questions.learningObjective: Explain why field is maximum at the surface
questions.stem: A beekeeper's notes ask why gravitational field is greatest at the surface of a uniform sphere.

answer.exemplar: At the surface all mass is enclosed, giving the maximum g; inside, enclosed mass grows slower than r^2 shrinks, so g is smaller.

questions.explanation: Enclosed mass grows as r^3 inside, so g ∝ r; at the surface r=R gives the peak. Beyond, inverse-square decay takes over.
questions.hint: Compare interior growth with exterior decay.

questions.stem: A satellite orbits at radius 8.0e6 m with speed 7.0 km/s; what is its centripetal acceleration in m/s^2?

options.text: Any speed works if thrust is applied.

options.text: The satellite mass would have to change.

questions.explanation: For a fixed radius, gravity must supply exactly mv^2/r, fixing v. Other speeds give non-circular orbits.

questions.stem: A beekeeper's notes ask why both bodies in a binary system orbit rather than just the lighter one.

answer.exemplar: Both bodies feel equal and opposite gravitational forces, so both accelerate and orbit their common centre of mass.

questions.explanation: Newton's third law ensures equal forces, so neither body can be treated as fixed. Both orbit the centre of mass.

questions.stem: A table lists circular speed 7.9 km/s and escape speed 11.2 km/s at the same radius; which speed is impossible for a closed orbit?

options.text: Neither, because any speed can orbit.
7.9 km/s, because it is too slow to orbit.
options.misconception: confuses circular speed with being too slow

options.text: Both, because only one speed can orbit.
11.2 km/s, because it escapes rather than orbits.

questions.explanation: Escape speed is not an orbital speed; at that speed the body leaves the planet. Circular speed sustains a closed orbit.

questions.learningObjective: Explain the shell theorem in words
questions.stem: A beekeeper's notes ask for a statement of the shell theorem for a hollow planet.

answer.exemplar: A uniform spherical shell attracts external masses as if all its mass were at the centre, and exerts no gravitational force on masses inside.

questions.explanation: This is the shell theorem: outside it acts like a point mass, inside the field is zero.
